شَقَذٌ : see شَقَذَانٌ. ―
-b2- مَا بِهِ شَقَذٌ وَلَا نَقَذٌ There is not in him any motion. (IAar, S, L.) ―
-b3- And, (L, K, in the CK ما به شَقْذٌ ولا نَقْذٌ,) as also ما ولا نُقْذُ ↓ به شُقْذٌ , (K,) There is not in it (namely, a commodity, or household furniture, L) any fault, or defect: and there is not in it (namely, language, or speech, L) any defect, imperfection, or unsoundness. (L, K. *) ―
-b4- And مَا لَهُ شَقَذٌ وَلَا نَقَذٌ He possesses not anything. (L, K.) ―
-b5- And مَا دُونَهُ شَقَذٌ وَلَا نَقَذٌ There is not anything to be feared, nor anything to be disliked, in the way to the attainment thereof. (Meyd, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
